questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Jhelum river originates from which spring in Jammu & Kashmir?
questions.explanation: The Jhelum rises at the Verinag spring in the Anantnag district. Kokernag and Achabal are other famous springs of south Kashmir but are not the source of the Jhelum, and Chashme Shahi is a Mughal garden spring in Srinagar, so only Verinag is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Kashmir Valley:

(i) The Jhelum is its principal river.
(ii) Srinagar is situated on the banks of the Jhelum.
(iii) The Wular Lake is fed by the Jhelum.
(iv) The valley has a hot desert climate.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Jhelum is the valley's main river, Srinagar sits on its banks, and it feeds the Wular Lake, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Kashmir Valley has a temperate climate with cold, snowy winters, not a hot desert climate, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous Mughal garden 'Shalimar Bagh' in Srinagar was built by:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh was laid out by Emperor Jahangir in 1619 for his wife Nur Jahan. Akbar and Babur predate the garden and did not build it, and while Shah Jahan added structures to Mughal gardens, the Shalimar Bagh of Srinagar is credited to Jahangir, so he is the correct answer.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes with their locations:

Column I:
(a) Wular Lake
(b) Dal Lake
(c) Pangong Lake
(d) Manasbal Lake

Column II:
(i) Srinagar
(ii) Ladakh
(iii) Bandipora
(iv) Ganderbal

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Wular Lake is in Bandipora, Dal Lake in Srinagar, Pangong in Ladakh and Manasbal in Ganderbal, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv). The other options misplace Pangong in Ganderbal or Dal in Bandipora, which contradicts the actual geography of these lakes.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which mountain pass connects the Kashmir Valley with the Ladakh region?
questions.explanation: Zoji La links the Kashmir Valley (Sonamarg) with Ladakh (Drass/Kargil). The Banihal Pass connects the valley with Jammu, the Pir Panjal Pass lies in the Pir Panjal range, and Khardung La is within Ladakh near Leh, so only Zoji La joins Kashmir to Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are tourist destinations located in Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) Gulmarg
(ii) Pahalgam
(iii) Nainital
(iv) Sonamarg

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg are all well-known hill destinations in Jammu & Kashmir, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Nainital is a hill station in Uttarakhand, not in J&K, so any option that includes Nainital is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Amarnath cave shrine in Jammu & Kashmir is dedicated to which deity?
questions.explanation: The Amarnath cave enshrines a naturally forming ice lingam worshipped as Lord Shiva. It is not associated with Vishnu, Rama or Krishna, whose major shrines lie elsewhere, so Lord Shiva is the correct deity for the Amarnath pilgrimage.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Chenab river originates within the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): The Chenab is formed by the confluence of the Chandra and Bhaga rivers in Himachal Pradesh.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: The reason is true: the Chenab forms from the Chandra and Bhaga rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh. This makes the assertion false, since the Chenab does not originate in the Kashmir Valley. Hence (A) is wrong while (R) is correct; the first two options fail because (A) is false, and the third fails because (R) is true.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which is the highest battlefield in the world, located in the Ladakh region?
questions.explanation: The Siachen Glacier is called the world's highest battlefield due to military posts at extreme altitudes. Kargil and Drass are towns associated with the 1999 conflict but are not the glacier, and Nubra is a valley in Ladakh, so only the Siachen Glacier fits the description.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the RTI Act:

(i) RTI stands for Right to Information.
(ii) It empowers citizens to seek information from public authorities.
(iii) The RTI Act was enacted in 2005.
(iv) It applies only to the central government.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: RTI means Right to Information, it lets citizens seek information from public authorities, and it was enacted in 2005, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Act applies to public authorities at both central and state levels, not only the central government, so any option with (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Jawahar Tunnel (Banihal Tunnel) provides an important road link connecting the Kashmir Valley with:
questions.explanation: The Jawahar Tunnel under the Banihal Pass links the Kashmir Valley with the Jammu region along the national highway. Leh and Kargil lie in Ladakh reached via Zoji La, and Anantnag is a district within the valley itself, so the tunnel's key connection is to Jammu.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the number of tourists (in lakhs) visiting a destination in Jammu & Kashmir:

2019 — 12
2020 — 4
2021 — 8
2022 — 15

In which year was the number of tourists the lowest?
questions.explanation: The 2020 figure of 4 lakh is the lowest of the four years, well below 8 lakh in 2021, 12 lakh in 2019 and 15 lakh in 2022. 2021 is the second lowest, not the least, while 2019 and 2022 are the highest, so 2020 saw the fewest tourists.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which river is the principal river of the Jammu region?
questions.explanation: The Chenab is the largest and principal river flowing through the Jammu region, powering major hydro projects. The Jhelum is the chief river of the Kashmir Valley, the Ravi flows along the border, and the Tawi is a smaller tributary through Jammu city, so the Chenab is the principal river.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following power projects with their rivers:

Column I:
(a) Uri Power Project
(b) Baglihar Dam
(c) Ranjit Sagar Dam
(d) Nimoo Bazgo Project

Column II:
(i) Chenab
(ii) Jhelum
(iii) Indus
(iv) Ravi

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Uri is on the Jhelum, Baglihar on the Chenab, Ranjit Sagar on the Ravi and Nimoo Bazgo on the Indus, giving (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii). The other options swap the Jhelum and Chenab or misplace the Ravi and Indus projects, which are factually incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Tulip Garden, the largest of its kind in Asia, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden, Asia's largest, is on the foothills of the Zabarwan range in Srinagar overlooking the Dal Lake. Jammu, Gulmarg and Pahalgam are known for other attractions but not this garden, so Srinagar is the correct location.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Indus Water Treaty was signed between India and Pakistan in the year __________.
questions.explanation: The Indus Water Treaty was signed in 1960 with the World Bank's mediation. 1947 is the year of Partition, 1950 saw the Constitution come into force, and 1965 was a year of war between the two countries, so none of them matches; 1960 is the correct year of the treaty.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which city served as the winter capital of the erstwhile state of Jammu & Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Jammu was the winter capital under the 'Darbar Move' system, while Srinagar was the summer capital. Leh is the headquarters of Ladakh and Anantnag is a district in the Kashmir Valley, so neither served as the winter capital, making Jammu correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indus Water Treaty:

(i) It was brokered by the World Bank.
(ii) The eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) were allocated to India.
(iii) The western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) were allocated to Pakistan.
(iv) It was signed in Srinagar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The World Bank brokered the treaty, the eastern rivers went to India and the western rivers to Pakistan, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the treaty was signed in Karachi, not Srinagar, so any option that includes (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Gulmarg is a popular skiing destination in Jammu & Kashmir.
Reason (R): Gulmarg is located in the Ladakh region at a very high altitude.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: The assertion is true: Gulmarg is a famous skiing resort with a high-altitude gondola. However the reason is false because Gulmarg lies in the Baramulla district of the Kashmir Valley, not in Ladakh. Hence (A) is correct but (R) is wrong; the first two options fail because (R) is false, and the last fails because (A) is true.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous Shankaracharya Temple, situated on a hilltop, overlooks which city?
questions.explanation: The Shankaracharya Temple stands on the Shankaracharya (Takht-e-Suleiman) hill overlooking Srinagar and the Dal Lake. Jammu, Leh and Anantnag have their own notable shrines, but the Shankaracharya Temple specifically overlooks Srinagar, making it the correct answer.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Saffron cultivation in Kashmir is chiefly associated with which town?
questions.explanation: Pampore, in the Pulwama district, is known as the saffron town of Kashmir and produces most of India's saffron. Sopore is famous for apples, while Baramulla and Kupwara are north Kashmir districts not primarily linked with saffron, so Pampore is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are major agricultural or horticultural products of Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) Apple
(ii) Saffron
(iii) Coffee
(iv) Walnut

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Apples, saffron and walnuts are all important products of J&K's temperate agriculture and horticulture, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Coffee is grown in the warm south Indian states like Karnataka, not in J&K's cool climate, so any option including coffee is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dachigam National Park near Srinagar is famous for which endangered species?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park is best known as the last refuge of the Hangul, the Kashmir stag. Snow leopards and ibex are found in the higher Ladakh ranges, and the musk deer inhabits other Himalayan forests, so the Hangul is the species specifically associated with Dachigam.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the climate of Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) The Kashmir Valley experiences cold winters with snowfall.
(ii) Ladakh has a cold desert climate.
(iii) The Jammu region has comparatively hotter summers.
(iv) Kashmir receives most of its rainfall from the southwest monsoon like the northern plains.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Kashmir has snowy winters, Ladakh is a cold desert, and Jammu has hotter summers, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because Kashmir receives much of its precipitation from western disturbances in winter rather than the southwest monsoon, so any option with (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which lake in Ladakh is known for changing colours and lies partly in India and partly in China?
questions.explanation: Pangong Tso is a high-altitude lake famous for its shifting blue shades, with a large part lying in Chinese-controlled territory. Tso Moriri lies entirely within India, while the Dal and Wular lakes are in the Kashmir Valley, so Pangong Tso is the correct answer.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tourist places with their features:

Column I:
(a) Gulmarg
(b) Sonamarg
(c) Pahalgam
(d) Patnitop

Column II:
(i) Meadow of Gold
(ii) Base for the Amarnath Yatra
(iii) Gondola cable car
(iv) Hill station in the Jammu region

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Gulmarg is famous for its Gondola, Sonamarg means 'Meadow of Gold', Pahalgam is a base for the Amarnath Yatra and Patnitop is a hill station near Jammu, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv). The other options swap the Gondola with the meadow or misplace Patnitop, which are incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Char Chinar', a small island with chinar trees, is located in which lake?
questions.explanation: Char Chinar is a well-known island in the Dal Lake of Srinagar, planted with four chinar trees. The Wular and Manasbal lakes and the adjoining Nagin Lake do not host this island, so the Dal Lake is the correct location of Char Chinar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ladakh receives heavy rainfall throughout the year.
Reason (R): Ladakh lies in the rain-shadow region of the Himalayas and is a cold desert.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: The reason is true: Ladakh lies in the Himalayan rain-shadow and is a cold desert with very little rainfall. This makes the assertion false, since Ladakh does not receive heavy year-round rain. Hence (A) is wrong while (R) is correct; the first two options fail because (A) is false, and the third fails because (R) is true.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The historical Mubarak Mandi Palace complex is located in which city of Jammu & Kashmir?
questions.explanation: The Mubarak Mandi Palace, once the royal residence of the Dogra rulers, is located in Jammu city. Srinagar has palaces and gardens of its own, Leh has the Leh Palace, and Udhampur is a separate district, so Mubarak Mandi is specifically in Jammu.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about power projects in Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) The Salal project is on the Chenab river.
(ii) The Uri project is on the Jhelum river.
(iii) Hydroelectricity is an important source of power in J&K.
(iv) Jammu & Kashmir has no potential for hydropower.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Salal project is on the Chenab, the Uri project on the Jhelum, and hydroelectricity is indeed a key power source in J&K, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because J&K has vast untapped hydropower potential on its rivers, so any option with (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the apple production (in lakh tonnes) of a Jammu & Kashmir district:

2019 — 15
2020 — 18
2021 — 20
2022 — 22

What is the total apple production over these four years?
questions.explanation: Total production = 15 + 18 + 20 + 22 = 75 lakh tonnes. Option 70 and 72 come from arithmetic slips in the addition, and 78 overstates the sum by three; only 75 correctly adds all four yearly figures, so it is the right total.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Hazratbal Shrine, which houses a sacred relic, is located in:
questions.explanation: The Hazratbal Shrine stands on the northern bank of the Dal Lake in Srinagar and preserves a relic believed to be of Prophet Muhammad. Jammu, Leh and Anantnag have other important shrines, but Hazratbal is specifically in Srinagar, making it the correct location.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are rivers that flow through Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) Jhelum
(ii) Chenab
(iii) Kaveri
(iv) Tawi

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Jhelum, Chenab and Tawi all flow through Jammu & Kashmir, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. The Kaveri is a river of southern India (Karnataka and Tamil Nadu) and does not flow through J&K, so any option that includes the Kaveri is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The abbreviation 'SKIMS', a premier hospital in Srinagar, stands for Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of:
questions.explanation: SKIMS stands for the Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, a major tertiary-care hospital in Srinagar. Management, marine and mountain sciences are unrelated fields not represented by this institute, so 'Medical Sciences' correctly expands the abbreviation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the history of Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) Maharaja Hari Singh was the last ruling Maharaja of the princely state.
(ii) The Instrument of Accession was signed in October 1947.
(iii) Zorawar Singh was a general associated with the conquest of Ladakh.
(iv) The Dogra dynasty ruled from Srinagar as its permanent and only capital.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hari Singh was the last Maharaja, the Instrument of Accession was signed in October 1947, and Zorawar Singh led campaigns into Ladakh, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Dogras used both Jammu and Srinagar under the Darbar Move rather than a single permanent capital, so any option with (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following personalities connected with Jammu & Kashmir with their fields:

Column I:
(a) Sheikh Abdullah
(b) Bilquis Mir
(c) Parvez Rasool
(d) Zorawar Singh

Column II:
(i) Cricket
(ii) Water sports (kayaking)
(iii) Politics
(iv) Military general

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Sheikh Abdullah was a political leader, Bilquis Mir is associated with water sports/kayaking, Parvez Rasool is a cricketer, and Zorawar Singh was a military general, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iv). The other options swap cricket with the general or politics with water sports, which are incorrect.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a cold desert region of India located in the Jammu & Kashmir / Ladakh area?
questions.explanation: Ladakh is a high-altitude cold desert with sparse rainfall and extreme temperatures. The Kashmir Valley has a temperate climate, Jammu is subtropical, and Doda is a mountainous district but not a cold desert, so Ladakh is the correct cold desert region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Tourism is important to the economy of Jammu & Kashmir.
Reason (R): Jammu & Kashmir shares its borders with Pakistan and China.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: tourism is a major economic sector of J&K, and the region does border Pakistan and China. However, sharing international borders is not the reason tourism is important (that owes to its scenic beauty and pilgrimage sites), so (R) does not explain (A). The other options fail because both statements are in fact true.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Vaishno Devi shrine is located in the Trikuta hills near which town?
questions.explanation: Pilgrims begin the trek to the Vaishno Devi shrine from Katra, the base town in the Reasi district. Udhampur and Samba are separate districts, and while the shrine falls within Reasi district, the specific base town is Katra, so Katra is the correct answer.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Kupwara, Baramulla and Anantnag are districts of which region of Jammu & Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Kupwara, Baramulla and Anantnag are all districts located within the Kashmir Valley. The Jammu region contains districts like Jammu and Udhampur, Ladakh comprises Leh and Kargil, and Pir Panjal is a mountain range, not an administrative region, so the Kashmir Valley is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Zojila tunnel, being built as one of Asia's longest road tunnels, will connect Ladakh with the:
questions.explanation: The Zojila tunnel will provide all-weather connectivity between Ladakh and the Kashmir Valley by bypassing the snow-blocked Zoji La pass. It does not directly link Ladakh to the Jammu region, the Punjab plains or Himachal, so the Kashmir Valley is the correct connection.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the rivers and lakes of Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) The Tawi river flows through Jammu city.
(ii) The Wular Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia.
(iii) The Jhelum drains into the Wular Lake.
(iv) The Dal Lake is a saltwater lake.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Tawi flows through Jammu, the Wular is among Asia's largest freshwater lakes, and the Jhelum drains into it, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Dal Lake is a freshwater lake, not saltwater, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are historical or heritage places located in Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) Martand Sun Temple
(ii) Mubarak Mandi
(iii) Konark Sun Temple
(iv) Hari Parbat Fort

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Martand Sun Temple, Mubarak Mandi and Hari Parbat Fort are all heritage sites in J&K, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. The Konark Sun Temple is in Odisha, not in J&K, so any option that includes Konark is wrong.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Martand Sun Temple, an ancient ruined temple in Kashmir, was built by which ruler?
questions.explanation: The Martand Sun Temple was built in the 8th century by Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty. Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah) and Avantivarman were later rulers linked with other works, and Ranjit Singh was a Sikh ruler of Punjab, so Lalitaditya is credited with Martand.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The largest freshwater lake in India, located in Jammu & Kashmir, is the __________ Lake.
questions.explanation: The Wular Lake in the Bandipora district is one of the largest freshwater lakes in India and Asia. The Dal and Nagin lakes in Srinagar and the smaller Manasbal Lake are all much smaller in area, so the Wular Lake correctly fills the blank.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following table shows the approximate length (in km) of major rivers associated with Jammu & Kashmir:

Jhelum — 725
Chenab — 960
Ravi — 720
Tawi — 141

Which of these rivers is the longest overall?
questions.explanation: At about 960 km the Chenab is the longest of the four rivers listed, ahead of the Jhelum at 725 km, the Ravi at 720 km and the Tawi at 141 km. The Jhelum is second and the Tawi by far the shortest, so the Chenab is the longest overall.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kheer Bhawani temple, an important pilgrimage site, is located in which district of the Kashmir Valley?
questions.explanation: The Kheer Bhawani temple is at Tulla Mulla in the Ganderbal district and is revered especially by Kashmiri Pandits. Baramulla and Kupwara are in north Kashmir and Kulgam in the south, none of which hosts this shrine, so Ganderbal is the correct district.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Kashmir Valley lies in a rain-shadow and therefore remains a hot desert.
Reason (R): The Pir Panjal range separates the Kashmir Valley from the Jammu plains.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: The reason is true: the Pir Panjal range does separate the Kashmir Valley from the Jammu plains. However the assertion is false because the Kashmir Valley has a temperate climate with snowfall, not a hot desert. Hence (A) is wrong while (R) is correct; the first two options fail because (A) is false, and the third fails because (R) is true.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan took place in which year?
questions.explanation: The Kargil conflict was fought in 1999 in the Kargil sector of Ladakh. 1998 was the year of India's Pokhran nuclear tests, 2001 saw the Parliament attack, and 1997 has no such event, so none of them matches; 1999 is the correct year of the Kargil war.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the administrative status of Jammu & Kashmir:

(i) Ladakh was carved out as a separate Union Territory in 2019.
(ii) Jammu & Kashmir became a Union Territory in 2019.
(iii) Leh and Kargil are districts of Ladakh.
(iv) Jammu & Kashmir continues to be a full-fledged state with its own legislature elected in 1947.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: In 2019 Ladakh became a separate Union Territory, Jammu & Kashmir was reorganised into a Union Territory, and Leh and Kargil are the districts of Ladakh, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because J&K ceased to be a full state in 2019, so any option including (iv) is wrong.
